why: What the workload suite is allowed to claim, declared rather than inferred.
The suite already knows the difference between a model that was VERIFIED
against a reference and one that was only EXECUTED, and until this file
existed that difference lived in prose on docs/source/designs/workload_suite.rst
where nothing could check it. Each model below names its tier on the ladder
examples/tinytpu/act/judge.py defines -- legal, correct, confirmed -- and a
model at the `confirmed` tier must carry the RTL measurement that earned it,
with the configuration it was measured at.
A measurement is declared with its configuration because this project's
most-repeated error is quoting a number from a configuration it was not
measured on: TPU_MAXDIM defaults to 64 and not 16, and TPU_QD defaulted to 8
until 63ee6ec7. gate.py compares the live build against these `config`
blocks and refuses to report a measurement whose configuration it is not
running -- it does not scale, interpolate or assume.
`quoted_in` is the association DECLARED rather than guessed. Matching a
number against a set of committed totals is decidable; working out which
cycle count a figure in prose refers to is not, so the page does not get
guessed at -- it gets told what it must contain.

source.provenance: Vitis cosim (xsim), ap_start to ap_done, -m_axi_latency 0, one csynth per burst width shared by every layer and every model, bit-exact against isa_ref over all MAXDIM*MAXDIM bytes of C.
source.transcribed: 2026-09-24, from the committed page. These rows are a RECORD of a measurement made in an earlier session, not a re-measurement: gate.py can check that they are self-consistent, that they belong to the configuration it is running, and that the page still quotes them, and it cannot check that xsim once printed them.

not_confirmed: Correct and not confirmed. Its programs agree with isa_ref on four
operand distributions and with PyTorch's own int8 epilogue chain on
every byte, and Vitis csim reports 0 / 4096 mismatches -- but no RTL
run of it has ever produced a cycle count.
This is limitations item 24. The re-check the QD=16 default invites has
already been made and is recorded on the page: six cosim runs over four
builds and both burst widths, including TPU_QD=16 (600 s bound, last
RTL progress at the first periodic report) and TPU_QD=32 (1500 s bound,
33.4 ms of simulated time, about ten million cycles on a program the
model prices at 22 000). QD=16 is what made mlp_tiny, mlp_deep and
mlp_small measurable at all; it does not make mlp_wide complete, so
Kt >= QD is not the whole rule.
